Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the clear signals on what success looks like. Quick recap + proposed next steps for the POC observability work so we can get aligned and start provisioning: 

Recap (from today)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference integration for a customer-facing payments use case (tokenization + verification flows) with focus on performance, reliability, and cost.
- Core success criteria called out by FintechX: <=250ms P95 inference latency for standard prompts, error rate <0.5%, and observable regression-free output quality across a set of 100 eval prompts.
- Timeline: 3-week POC window preferred; kickoff asap once credentials and test traffic are available.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Observability plan (see attached draft dashboard): pin metrics & dashboards we'll monitor during the POC.
2) Access: please provide a service account or API token with staging dataset access and a sample of 200 representative prompts.
3) Kickoff: 30-45m kickoff next week to hand off creds and align owners.

I attached a one-page dashboard PDF with the initial set of metrics and proposed owner assignments. I'll follow up with a detailed plan this week that includes tracing, log export, and alert thresholds.

Attachments: poc-observability-dashboard.pdf

Thanks — available next Tue/Wed morning PT for kickoff.

— Marissa

Subject: Re: POC Observability follow-up — Observability Plan (details & owners)

Emily / Lucas — thanks. Below is the detailed observability plan I promised. This will be our working checklist for the 3-week POC.

High-level objective
- Provide end-to-end visibility into model inference behavior (latency, errors, throughput), cost drivers (tokens per request, batching efficiency), and output quality (eval set pass rate). Enable both teams to quickly triage regressions and confirm SLA targets.

Key dashboards (we'll provide Looker/Datadog/Grafana templates)
- POC Overview: P50/P95/P99 latency, successful request rate, requests per minute, average tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens.
- Error/Failures: error rate by type (model errors, network, 4xx/5xx), per-endpoint error heatmap, stack traces for server-side failures.
- Quality Eval: rolling eval pass/fail on the 100 prompt set, diff view vs baseline, top failure examples (with input + model output).
- Resource Utilization: GPU utilization, VRAM pressure, CPU, and disk I/O for the serving nodes.
- Cache & Batching: KV cache hit rate, average batch size, and batching latency distribution.

Tracing & logs
- Tracing: we will instrument request traces (distributed trace IDs) to correlate client request -> routing -> model call -> response. Traces will capture per-hop latencies (routing, queuing, model inference).
- Logs: structured request/response logs (redacted PII), debug-level logs on failed requests, and model fallback events. We'll export logs to your staging GCP project or an S3 bucket (your preference).

Metrics to monitor (initial set)
- Latency: P50, P95, P99 inference latency (ms) per route
- Errors: total error rate (%), 4xx vs 5xx breakdown, model-exception rate
- Throughput: requests/sec, tokens/sec
- Cost: tokens per request, estimated $/1k tokens (hosted)
- Quality: eval pass rate (%), rolling 24h failure rate on eval set
- Ops: GPU utilization (%), queue depth, batch size avg
- Caching: KV cache hit rate (%)

Success criteria (for sign-off)
1) Performance: P95 inference latency <= 250ms for standard prompts under the agreed test load (TBD RPS).
2) Reliability: total error rate < 0.5% during a 24h soak with representative traffic.
3) Quality: >= 95% pass rate on the 100-eval prompt set, with no regressions vs baseline.
4) Observability: dashboards populated and alerting (basic thresholds) operational; logs + traces exported to FintechX staging.

Ownership & responsibilities
- Redwood: provide dashboard templates, instrument traces on our side, export hooks for logs, and a short runbook for triage. We'll also run a performance sweep during week 2. (Owners: Marcus Lin for dashboards, Aditya Rao for tracing/export.)
- FintechX: provide API token/service account for staging, a sample of 200 prompts and target RPS test profile, and access to the staging GCP/S3 location for logs. (Owner: Emily)

Timeline (3-week plan)
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): SOW + creds exchanged; baseline prompts shared.
- Week 1 (integration & baseline): instrumenting, dashboards up, smoke tests.
- Week 2 (stress & soak): run target RPS, iterate on batching/caching configs, capture metrics.
- Week 3 (evaluation & sign-off): run eval set, finalize reports, sign-off or next steps.

Evaluation & deliverables
- Daily dashboard snapshots, runbook + post-POC report with metrics and recommendations (quantified cost/latency tradeoffs).

Immediate asks for kickoff
1) FintechX to confirm preferred log export (GCP staging project vs S3) and provide write access.
2) Service account or API key with staging dataset access.
3) 200 sample prompts (CSV) + target RPS profile (e.g., 5 rps steady-state, 20 rps peak).

Proposed kickoff times: Wed 2026-06-23 09:00-09:45 PT or 11:00-11:45 PT. Let us know which works.

Link: POC dashboard template (view + copy): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_observability

Attachments: poc-observability-dashboard.pdf, poc-sow-redlines.docx

I'll be online to join the kickoff and will lead the post-POC report. Marcus (cc) will own dashboard creation and Aditya will handle tracing/export.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

— Marissa
